subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: Should OpenClaw reclaim live current-PID session locks during startup/recovery when the lock is not tracked in the fresh in-process lock manager, or preserve them until a stricter ownership signal proves they are orphaned?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally avoid cutting off live OpenClaw-owned transcript writers, while field reports show that same safety rule can leave sessions wedged when the process survives but lock ownership state is lost.

options.title: Land Narrow Self-Lock Reclaim
options.body: Review the linked PR or a replacement that reclaims only untracked current-PID locks with enough owner evidence, and add regression coverage for startup and restart-recovery cleanup.

options.title: Require Stronger Lease Signal First
options.body: Keep live OpenClaw-owned locks preserved until a heartbeat, owner operation id, or lock-manager snapshot makes false-positive reclaim safer.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Session-Lock Design
options.body: Move this issue under the broader multi-agent/session-lock reliability umbrella and solve same-PID lock recovery together with lock heartbeat and delivery guarantees.

recommendation.title: Land Narrow Self-Lock Reclaim
recommendation.body: Review the linked PR or a replacement that reclaims only untracked current-PID locks with enough owner evidence, and add regression coverage for startup and restart-recovery cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision balances session-data safety against operator recovery and aligns with prior steipete history in the lock policy and product-boundary area.
